panels.description: % of time the service responded successfully over the selected window. SLO target: 99.9%. Red = SLO breach.
panels.title: Availability

panels.description: % of requests returning 5xx errors. SLO budget: <1%. >5% triggers P1 incident.
panels.title: Error Rate

panels.description: 99th-percentile request duration. Warn: >200 ms. Alert: >500 ms. Correlate spikes with deploy events.
panels.title: P99 Latency

panels.description: Total inbound requests per second across all selected services. No threshold color is applied here — throughput alone is neither good nor bad without a baseline. A spike could mean healthy growth or a traffic flood. Compare against historical trends rather than a fixed threshold.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Inbound requests per second by service. Sudden drops may indicate an availability issue.
panels.title: Request Rate

panels.description: Error % over time. The shaded red area marks the SLO breach zone (>5%). Yellow band = warning zone (1–5%).
panels.title: Error Rate

### Service Drill-Down
Filtered to **$service** in **$env** / **$region**. Use the filters above to scope to a specific service. Each chart shows the last selected time range.

panels.description: Inbound requests per second for the selected service(s). Use this to detect traffic anomalies and confirm deploys.
panels.title: Request Rate

panels.description: Latency percentiles. P99 > 500 ms = alert. P50 tracks the median user experience. Wide spread between P50 and P99 = tail latency problem.
panels.title: Latency Percentiles (P50 / P95 / P99)

panels.description: Error % over time for the selected service. SLO: <1%. Consistently >5% = SLO breach. Compare with latency to distinguish error vs slowness.
panels.title: Error Rate

options.content:
### Infrastructure Health
Host-level resource metrics for **$env** / **$region**. Thresholds: CPU warns at **70%**, alerts at **90%**. Memory warns at **80%**, alerts at **95%**. Correlate spikes here with service latency above.

panels.description: CPU utilization across hosts. Dashed lines mark Warning (70%) and Critical (90%) thresholds. Sustained >70% warrants scaling review.
panels.title: CPU Usage

panels.description: RAM consumption per host as a percentage of total. Warning: 6 GiB / Critical: 7 GiB. Sustained pressure above warning often precedes OOM kills.
panels.title: Memory Usage

panels.description: Inbound network throughput per host. Unexpected spikes may indicate backup jobs, log shipping storms, or noisy neighbours.
panels.title: Network Received

panels.description: Outbound network throughput per host. Sustained elevation above baseline warrants investigation — common causes include bulk data exports, replication lag catch-up, or data exfiltration.
panels.title: Network Transmitted

## 📖 Runbooks

**High Error Rate (>1%)**
[→ Error Rate SLO Burn](https://runbook.internal/error-rate)

**High Latency (P99 >200 ms)**
[→ Latency SLO Burn](https://runbook.internal/latency)

**Service Unavailable**
[→ Availability Runbook](https://runbook.internal/availability)

**Node CPU / Memory**
[→ Infrastructure Issues](https://runbook.internal/node)

**Payment Service**
[→ Payment Runbook](https://runbook.internal/payment)

---

_All runbooks live in Confluence under [Platform › Runbooks](https://confluence.internal/platform)_

## 📞 Escalation

**Step 1:** Check this dashboard for scope
**Step 2:** Join **#platform-incidents** on Slack
**Step 3:** Page on-call via [PagerDuty](https://pagerduty.com)
**Step 4:** If no response in 5 min → escalate to manager

---

**Severity guide**

| Level | Condition |
|---|---|
| P0 | Production down / data loss |
| P1 | >5% error rate or >500 ms P99 |
| P2 | Single service degraded |
| P3 | Non-urgent, business hours |

---

_For postmortems see [Incidents](https://incidents.internal)_
